item.title: Djibouti, Republic of the Congo foreign ministers to visit China, underscoring deepening China-Africa cooperation: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18 15:44:00
Closer cooperation. Illustration: Liu Rui/GT The foreign ministers of Djibouti and the Republic of the Congo are set to begin official visits to China on Monday. A Chinese expert said the visits uncerscore deepening China-Africa cooperation in security, infrastructure and economic development, help drive Africa's economic growth and strengthen solidarity among Global South countries amid rising geopolitical tensions. Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Djibouti Abdoulkader Houssein Omar will pay an official visit to China from October 19 to 25, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Friday, per Xinhua News Agency. Minister of Foreign Affairs, La Francophonie and Congolese Abroad of the Republic of the Congo Constant-Serge Bounda will pay an official visit to China from October 19 to 25, the spokesperson said. According to the spokesperson, the two foreign ministers are at the invitation of Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, who is also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee. Amid rising protectionism, unilateralism and intensifying geopolitical competition, China-Africa relations play an increasingly important role in boosting confidence among developing countries and setting an example for Global South cooperation, Song Wei, a professor at the School of International Relations and Diplomacy at Beijing Foreign Studies University, told the Global Times. In the security sphere, China is expected to deepen cooperation with Djibouti in capacity building, military training and information sharing, helping strengthen the country's security capabilities and contribute to regional stability, Song said. Meanwhile, China will continue to expand cooperation with African countries in infrastructure and mineral resources, encouraging more Chinese investment and cross-border infrastructure projects to promote regional economic integration and inject fresh momentum into Africa's development, Song noted. This year marks the 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and African nations. Over the past seven decades, the friendship has been passed down from generation to generation, and bilateral ties have achieved leapfrog development, per Xinhua. Over the past year, China has intensified practical cooperation with African partners under the Belt and Road Initiative. China has carried out upgrades and renovations at the old Nacala Port in Mozambique, renewed the technical service agreement for the Addis Ababa-Djibouti Railway, and completed track-laying for Africa's first heavy-haul desert railway, further strengthening the continent's connectivity foundations. In 2025, China and the Republic of the Congo upgraded bilateral ties to a high-level community with a shared future. President of the Republic of the Congo Denis Sassou Nguesso said that the elevation of bilateral relations has established a new framework for common prosperity and development of the two countries. Amid intensifying global geopolitical competition, China-Africa cooperation could help Global South countries build consensus, strengthen strategic mutual trust and explore independent development paths through deeper economic and development cooperation, said Song. The expert noted that China-Africa cooperation rests on strong economic complementarities, shared aspirations for modernization and independent development, and longstanding friendship. These factors have provided a solid foundation for further deepening practical cooperation between the two sides.

item.title: China unveils first 100,000-card AI supercluster hardware, showcases 10 frontier research applications
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18 14:27:00
Visitors tour the exhibition hall of Sugon 8000, China's first fully homegrown 100,000-card AI supercluster, at the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai on July 20, 2026. Photo: VCG The physical system of China's first artificial intelligence (AI) supercluster capable of supporting over 100,000 domestically developed computing cards, also known as Sugon 8000, debuted at the ongoing China National Annual Conference on High Performance Computing, CCTV News reported on Sunday. A 100,000-card cluster means interconnecting 100,000 AI accelerator cards at high speed. But scale is not its most impressive feature. Sugon 8000 is a computing system built explicitly around the native convergence of supercomputing and intelligent computing within a unified architecture. It can run both the highest-precision scientific computing and large model training and inference, according to CCTV News. The system marks a step toward scaling AI infrastructure construction is from the 10,000-card level to 100,000-card deployment. Connected to national integrated computing network through the National Supercomputing Internet, the system will provide accessible, efficient and convenient computing services to research institutions, universities, enterprises and individual users, Sugon said. By integrating high-performance computing (HPC) and AI computing, Sugon 8000 enables computing resources to be allocated according to the requirements of different tasks. This helps improve resource efficiency while meeting the needs of diverse scientific and industrial applications, Liu Gang, director of the Institute of Economic Research at Nankai University, told the Global Times on Sunday. Ma Jihua, a senior telecommunications analyst, said the successful deployment of Sugon 8000 has provided a reference for building domestic AI infrastructure at the 100,000-accelerator scale. "Such systems require more than simply connecting large numbers of chips: High-speed interconnects, storage throughput, liquid cooling, workload scheduling and long-term stability all pose major engineering challenges," Ma said. The system's rollout indicates that domestic computing infrastructure is moving toward larger-scale deployment and that integrated HPC-AI capabilities are progressing from construction to practical use, with the potential to support scientific breakthroughs and industrial applications, Ma said. During the National Annual Conference on High Performance Computing, Sugon presented results from 10 advanced research applications using Sugon 8000, ranging from studies of material properties at microscopic scales to simulations of celestial bodies, covering fields including commercial aerospace, meteorology and oceanography, agricultural breeding, energy exploration and engineering R&D. Several studies have achieved world-first breakthroughs, pointing to a clear trend of domestic advanced computing power accelerating its entry into industrial applications, according to media reports. To date, more than 300 key applications have been extensively optimized for Sugon 8000, spanning more than 30 research and industrial fields, with over 20 running on the full system. As AI technology penetrates every sector, computing systems must simultaneously support model training, data analysis and scientific simulation. Domestic heterogeneous computing, represented by Sugon 8000, offers advantages such as unified scheduling and high scaling efficiency and is expected to become a new type of infrastructure enabling enterprises to cut R&D costs, improve efficiency and shorten innovation cycles.

item.title: China's space station marks new 'harvest season,' aims to grow two generations of rice in orbit for first time
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18 13:16:00
Picture of China's space station rice experiment. Photo: China Central Television China's space station has welcomed a new "autumn harvest," with astronauts collecting, sowing and storing a new batch of rice experiment samples last week, marking further progress in research on rice cultivation in space, CCTV News reported on Sunday. The research project, which focuses on the molecular mechanisms regulating multigenerational genetic stability and environmental adaptability of rice in space, is progressing smoothly, according to the media report. The latest experiment is expected to grow two generations of rice in orbit for the first time, helping researchers understand the mechanisms through which prolonged exposure to microgravity affects the genetic stability of rice. In addition to the rice experiment, the astronauts conducted touch-interaction tests with Xiaohang, their robotic companion aboard the space station. The tests collected data on the robot's movements in response to different types of physical contact, providing data to improve its motion planning for future operations in orbit. The crew also completed assessments of emergency decision-making capabilities and tests of their emotional states in orbit. The data collected will be used to investigate how astronauts' emergency decision-making abilities and emotional states change during long-duration space missions. As part of a research project on musculoskeletal loading during exercise, the astronauts measured Achilles tendon stiffness, conducted biomechanical tests of the lower limbs, and assessed muscle and tendon characteristics. By collecting plantar pressure, joint kinematics data and exercise images during running and resistance exercises under different loading conditions in orbit, researchers aim to establish relationships between these data and muscle parameters, while identifying changes in muscle-tendon interactions. In another experiment examining changes in muscle groups, the astronauts used force-measuring equipment to conduct grip strength tests and ultrasound diagnostic equipment to examine important antigravity muscles, including the soleus, collecting relevant data. The crew also completed sample replacements in the experimental chamber of the containerless materials processing cabinet and maintenance of electrodes in its axial mechanism, in accordance with the experimental schedule. Last week, the three astronauts completed scheduled in-orbit medical rescue training, reinforcing their understanding of rescue procedures including how to apply force in a microgravity environment, according to the CCTV report. They also completed a full-system pressure emergency drill, simulating the entire emergency response process in the event of a loss of pressure inside the space station. The exercise helped strengthen the crew's emergency response capabilities and coordination between the space station and ground teams. Routine maintenance of the space station platform and crew health management also continued. The astronauts maintained equipment in the regenerative life-support system, cleaned the cabin environment and exercised according to schedule to maintain their physical and mental well-being. China's national space laboratory is expected to yield more scientific research achievements as experiments continue aboard the space station. Global Times

item.title: Chinese robotics firms race to roll out components and data systems, helping robots perceive, understand, interact with real world
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18 13:13:00
A humanoid robot uses Hesai Group's Kosmo spatial camera to scan a store in Shanghai on Wednesday. Photo: Li Xuanmin/Global Times At the Humanoid Robot Data Training Center in Beijing's western Shijingshan District, dozens of robots stood in their workrooms, learning how to pick up an object steadily and quickly. This is not a simple task - the robot must "see" the object, gauge its distance and angle, and control the force exerted by its fingers. Motion-capture systems, which convert human movements into training data, are insufficient to help these robots mature. To perform reliably across different objects and environments, robots need more precise 3D spatial perception, more sensitive tactile feedback, more dexterous end effectors, and data technologies capable of reconstructing and simulating the real world. As China's humanoid robots move from labs to factories and downstream competition increasingly centers on their ability to perceive and interact with the real world, every grasp at the Shijingshan training facility highlights the pressing need for more advanced supporting technologies and hardware devices. In this context, Chinese companies have been racing to roll out new products across upstream segments -from sensing hardware and dexterous hands to drive systems and data infrastructure, aiming to capitalize on this emerging opportunity while strengthening the homegrown embodied AI supply chain. "China's manufacturing of downstream humanoid robot is quite crowded now, there are still many business opportunities upstream, particularly in the perception layer which centered on enhancing embodied AI's perception and manipulation capabilities," Liu Shaoshan, director of Embodied AI at the Shenzhen Institute of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics for Society, told the Global Times. Behind this shift lies not only growing demand for robot applications, but also a change in the logic of industrial competition. As robots become more agile, the capacity to accurately understand their environment, perceive objects, and reliably complete tasks is becoming one of the key factors that determine their commercial value. Visual perception is one of the core technologies for robots. In line with the trend, physical AI infrastructure company Hesai Group on Wednesday launched Kosmo, a 3D world data engine. Kosmo combines Kosmo One, the world's first AI spatial camera, with the Kosmo World cloud platform to transform physical environments into high-fidelity 3D digital spaces for robot training, model development and immersive content creation. Li Yifan, co-founder and CEO of Hesai, said that there has been a surging demand for devices like Kosmo amid large-scale deployment of physical AI. The Kosmo devices were delivered to the first batch of customers in July this year, having securing orders from downstream companies including Galbot, engaging about 200 partners. Li noted that many current humanoid robots have yet to demonstrate a path toward general-purpose robots. "A robot that can dance does not necessarily have value, and a number of robots are still unable to complete real tasks. Some also does not in itself represent an upgrade in automation, failing to go beyond traditional automation such as parcel-sorting robots or cooking robots," Li told the Global Times. In this context, he stressed that the build-up of the infrastructure for physical AI has only just begun, and to facilitate the process, two key issues need to be properly addressed - how machines can act upon the real world, and how AI can obtain high-quality, sufficient volumes of real-world data. "Making robot smarter involves a large amount of investment, whether in large model, computing power or training data. In hardware part, it is about acting as the 'eyes' and 'muscles,' and enable the humanoid robots to execute more efficiently," Li explained. Hesai is not alone in the Chinese suppliers' moves to capitalize on this rapid-surging robotic upstream market demand. Orbbec, a high-tech firm based in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province specializing in 3D visual sensing technology, has been rolling out more of its EGO data collection devices this year, the Global Times learned from the company. The heat-mounted device records the wearer's perspective and movements, generating data for training large AI models used in robotics. "The demands from robotic companies have become more diversified, and we have customized our technologies accordingly. For example, service robots operate in environments with strong lighting, complex textures and sudden crowds. Our company analyzed on-site data and adjusted algorithms to solve the problem of robot operation under extreme lighting conditions. For sweeping robots, we provide an infrared active fill-light solution so that they can identify tiny objects even in nighttime," Zhao Jiyu, the company's marketing director, told the Global Times. Industry insiders believe that one of the reasons Chinese upstream device makers can respond swiftly to demands from the robotics supply chain lies in the rich experience they have accumulated in the rounds of tech wave - for example the consumer electronics boom and autonomous driving. "The core components of humanoid robots and autonomous driving overlap to a significant level of extent, enabling Chinese hardware suppliers to adapt to potential business demands more quickly while bringing down the costs further," Liu said. He also noted that downstream mass production of humanoid robots is "achievable" by building on automakers' production lines. Across the upstream, core component segments in China such as tactile sensors, dexterous hands and joint modules continued to attract additional capital this year, industry insiders said. "These developments are driven by demand from the downstream sector. As downstream applications become increasingly diverse, they in turn are feeding back into the upstream, requiring better components to support them," Liu said. He added that this is a very "unique" phenomenon in China as the country has the world's most comprehensive supply chain, with relatively easy access to parts in a wide variety of forms, which provides favorable conditions for the rapid iteration of humanoid robot perception-layer products. Analysts believe that China's robotics edge makes it probably the only country in the world capable of meeting real-world demand across all layers of humanoid robots at a competitive cost. According to IDC data, the global humanoid robot shipments approached 25,000 units in the first half of 2026, a year-on-year increase of 432.1 percent .Among which, China's shipment accounted for about 77.9 percent of the global market. According to Li, a single humanoid robot requires over 100 actuation modules, which refers to joint actuation units that drive robots' movement. And industry estimates suggest that when the global total of humanoid robots reaches 10 billion units, demand for actuation modules could reach 1 trillion sets.

item.title: Olympic champion Tola sets China's fastest marathon time with Beijing victory
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18 12:13:00
Runners participate in the Beijing Marathon on October 18, 2026 in Beijing. Photo: Courtesy of Beijing Marathon organizers Ethiopia's reigning Olympic marathon champion Tamirat Tola won the 2026 Beijing Marathon on Sunday in 2:03:10, setting a course record and the fastest time ever recorded at a marathon held in China. The 35-year-old's performance at the Beijing Marathon, which also hosted the National Marathon Championships, beat the previous course record of 2:07:06 by almost four minutes. Tola's winning time surpassed the previous fastest time recorded in a marathon in China, 2:05:35, set by Kenyan runner Philimon Kiptoo Kipchumba at the 2023 Shanghai Marathon. The result also underlined Tola's status as one of the leading marathon runners of his generation. He won the men's marathon at the 2022 World Athletics Championships in 2:05:36, then claimed Olympic gold at the Paris 2024 Games in an Olympic-record time of 2:06:26. With Beijing set to host the 2027 World Athletics Championships, 12 years after the 2015 edition, Tola's record could face a new challenge next year. Rain on Saturday gave way to cool, clear conditions for Sunday's race. The race began at Tian'anmen Square, with 32,000 runners taking part. Tola's record-setting victory set a new benchmark for the Beijing Marathon and brought the fastest marathon time recorded in China into the 2:03 range. The event is one of the country's major mass-participation road races, bringing international elite runners together with domestic competitors. Under the Beijing Marathon's prize policy, the men's and women's champions each receive $50,000. An additional 60,000 yuan ($8,967) is available to a champion who breaks the event's course record. Kenyan runner Sabastian Sawe, who made history in April by becoming the first man to run an official marathon in under 2 hours in London, was also in Beijing during the marathon weekend, according to media reports. He visited Peking University, where he shared his experiences and training insights with the young Chinese runners, offering a message to young runners just starting out: "Stay passionate, be patient and remain disciplined."

item.title: Croatian PM meets Chinese FM, voices willingness to expand bilateral cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18 09:47:00
Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic meets with visiting Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, in Zagreb, Croatia, Oct. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Peng Ziyang) Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic met with visiting Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi here on Saturday, expressing Croatia's willingness to further expand cooperation with China. During the meeting, Plenkovic asked Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, to convey his sincere greetings to the Chinese leadership, saying that he looks forward to visiting China at an early date and meeting with the leadership. Relations between Croatia and China have continued to improve, underpinned by mutual respect and sincere cooperation, Plenkovic said. Chinese enterprises have participated in infrastructure projects in Croatia, including roads, bridges and tunnels, he said, noting that the Peljesac Bridge has played a significant role in improving connectivity between different parts of the country. The Croatian side highly appreciates these contributions and welcomes continued participation of Chinese enterprises in the country's development, he said. Croatia is willing to further expand cooperation with China in such areas as tourism, photovoltaics and wind power, he added. The prime minister also welcomes the launch of direct flights between Croatia and China, looking forward to closer exchanges between their peoples. Stressing that Croatia attaches great importance to cooperation with China under the China-Central and Eastern European Countries (CEECs) framework and the Belt and Road Initiative, Plenkovic said Croatia is willing to continue contributing to these efforts and looks forward to the early resumption of CEEC-China leaders' meeting mechanism to create new opportunities for closer high-level exchanges between the two sides. For his part, Wang conveyed the Chinese leadership's good wishes to Plenkovic and welcomed him to visit China at a mutually convenient time. Wang said China was among the first major countries to establish diplomatic relations with Croatia, adding that bilateral relations have enjoyed healthy, steady and sustainable development under the strategic guidance of the two countries' leaders. China and Croatia treat each other with sincerity and mutual respect and have established a mature, long-term comprehensive cooperative partnership, Wang said, noting that this has been the right choice made by both sides. China is willing to further elevate bilateral relations on this foundation, he added. Moreover, Wang said China cherishes its traditional friendship with Croatia and is willing to translate it into a strong driving force for bilateral relations in the new era. Wang also said China respects the choices of the Croatian people and Croatia's governance model, and is willing to deepen mutually beneficial cooperation to support each other's development and revitalization. China values people-to-people and cultural exchanges with Croatia and has introduced measures, including unilateral visa-free access and direct flights, to facilitate travel and enhance mutual understanding between the two peoples, Wang stressed. In addition, Wang noted that China firmly believes that China and the European Union (EU) are partners, not rivals. China supports European integration and Croatia's efforts to achieve faster development through this process, and hopes Croatia will play a constructive role in deepening China-EU cooperation, Wang added. Meanwhile, Wang stressed that China and CEECs share a practical need to strengthen exchanges and cooperation. Such cooperation is entirely open and transparent and contributes to European integration, he said. China is willing to strengthen cooperation with interested countries in the region through established mechanisms, Wang said, noting that China appreciates Croatia's positive attitude in this regard and is ready to use the 15th anniversary of the China-CEEC cooperation mechanism next year as an opportunity to reinvigorate mutually beneficial cooperation between the two sides. The two sides also exchanged views on China-EU economic and trade relations. Plenkovic said that EU countries, including Croatia, have concerns about trade imbalances. Participants at the recent EU summit spoke positively of the consensus reached through the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism and expressed hope that the two sides would continue to strengthen communication and dialogue to properly address their differences, he said. Wang said that trade issues between China and the EU stem from the international division of labor and market demand. Imports of high-quality, competitively priced Chinese goods benefit European consumers and help curb inflation, reflecting demand in the European market, and there is no so-called "overcapacity" problem, he noted. China is willing to import more high-value-added products from Europe and hopes the EU will ease restrictions on exports to China, Wang said. China is committed to promoting balanced growth in bilateral trade, with both sides moving forward rather than backward and expanding shared benefits rather than diminishing them, he added. He also said China is ready to strengthen dialogue with the EU on the basis of equality and mutual benefit, jointly uphold free trade and advance open and inclusive economic globalization. Meanwhile, Plenkovic briefed Wang on the situation in the Western Balkans. Wang said that China does not interfere in the internal affairs of countries in the region and hopes that all countries will enhance understanding, rebuild mutual trust and coexist in harmony through dialogue. China is willing to play a constructive role in line with the needs of countries in the region, he added. Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic meets with visiting Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, in Zagreb, Croatia, Oct. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Peng Ziyang)

item.title: Paraguay tech minister's response to China's countermeasures a deliberate attempt to shift responsibility
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17 16:28:00
Illustration: Liu Xiangya/GT Days after China announced countermeasures against Paraguay's Minister of Information and Communication Technologies Gustavo Emigdio Villate Samaniego over his wrong moves on the Taiwan question, he wrote lengthy posts on social media, which Chinese experts describe as an attempt to shift responsibility by framing the move over his own misconduct as targeting the entire country. In a post on his X account, Villate called the countermeasures “a certification that what we have been doing since 2023 is the correct path.” He also declared that Paraguay's relationship with the Taiwan region would "never be on the table as a bargaining chip." His remarks may sound defiant, but they turn cause and effect on their head: They recast interference in China's internal affairs as "sovereign diplomacy," and portray collusion with separatist forces as "cooperation between two democracies." Here is why China took the countermeasures against Villate and Belize Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade Francis Fonseca. In announcing the measures, a spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry pointed out that certain politicians in Paraguay and Belize willingly serve as chess pieces for Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities in their pursuit of independence by soliciting external support. "Their visits to Taiwan and reception of 'Taiwan independence' separatist forces in their countries constitute severe interference in China's internal affairs. They also attacked and smeared China by spreading the 'Chinese cyberattack' disinformation, causing egregious impact in the world," the spokesperson said. Apparently, the word that apparently struck a nerve with Villate was chess piece, or "pawn" as he puts it in his social media post. Villate’s decision to speak out loudly several days after the countermeasures were announced was an attempt to salvage his credibility after being exposed for his collusion with “Taiwan independence” separatist forces, Xin Qiang, director of the Taiwan Studies Center at Fudan University, told the Global Times on Monday, adding that Villate is putting on a stunt for people in Paraguay and DPP authorities to gain support. Villate seeks to turn China’s countermeasures against him into a political narrative about Paraguay "defending its right." Yet his refusal to reflect on his erroneous actions, and his determination to "accelerate" them, only further reinforce the impression that he is acting as a “pawn.” Villate also sought to frame his attempt to pursue certain so-called technology cooperation projects with DPP authorities as being in the interest of Paraguay, despite what experts describe as limited benefits and enormous costs in various fields. “Villate wants to convince people that his actions will bring prosperity to Paraguay, but there is no such thing as a free lunch,” Zhang Wensheng, deputy dean and a professor at the Taiwan Research Institute at Xiamen University, told the Global Times, adding that the move actually puts Paraguay's national interests and its people's welfare at risk. For years, voices within Paraguay's agricultural sector have called for reconsidering the country's diplomatic policy, hoping to gain access to China's market for beef, soybeans and other products. For a developing country seeking to expand agricultural exports, attract investment and upgrade its industries, the absence of normal diplomatic relations with one of the world's largest economies creates tangible obstacles. There is one thing Villate gets right: Beijing's message "deserves careful reading." Unfortunately, he has read it entirely backward. Being the only country in South America that still maintains so-called diplomatic relations with the Taiwan authorities is hardly a badge to boast about. Rather, it highlights how far Paraguay has moved against the prevailing international trend. More troublingly, the erroneous actions of certain politicians like Villate will also be borne by the country and its people. Ordinary people across the world want to pursue better lives through good jobs and development rather than by interfering in other countries’ internal affairs. Binding one's future to "Taiwan independence" separatist forces is not a path toward greater autonomy. It is a dead end that risks forfeiting development opportunities and leaving a country increasingly isolated internationally. The author is a reporter with the Global Times. opinion@globaltimes.com.cn

item.title: No bullying the small, no blackmail by the small: China's South China Sea rule
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16 18:11:00
Philippines South China Sea Illustration: Liu Xidan/Global Times Recent remarks by Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan have been portrayed in Manila as a threat. In fact, they restate a consistent Chinese position: firm defense of territorial sovereignty and maritime rights, together with a preference for peace, restraint and managing differences through direct dialogue. In the South China Sea, China will not use its size to bully the small, nor allow the Philippines to use its smallness to blackmail the strong. China’s approach to territorial and maritime disputes has remained stable for decades. It safeguards its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights while consistently advocating peaceful settlement through bilateral negotiation and consultation. This principle applies not only to the South China Sea but also to other territorial and maritime questions involving its neighbors. The disputes between China and the Philippines have a long history. China maintains that they stem primarily from the Philippines’ occupation of eight features in China’s Nansha Islands beginning in the 1970s and its subsequent claim over Huangyan Island. Overlapping maritime claims also emerged as the international law of the sea developed. Successive Philippine administrations have repeatedly taken actions that have aggravated tensions, including arrests of fishermen from the Chinese mainland and Taiwan, and the unilateral initiation of the South China Sea arbitration case, which China opposed as contrary to prior bilateral understandings and the principle of state consent. China regards its responses to infringement and provocation as legitimate measures to defend its rights. The equality of states under the United Nations Charter and general international law does not give any country a free hand to manufacture incidents at sea. Where a state has illegally occupied another state’s territory, the latter retains, in principle, the right of self-defense. China has exercised considerable restraint, prioritizing regional stability and preserving space for dialogue. That restraint should not be mistaken for the absence of limits. The disparity in national strength, particularly maritime capabilities, between China and the Philippines is an objective fact. Manila cannot expect its repeated provocations, public smearing, and the suspension of military communication channels to be met indefinitely with silence. China has treated the Philippines as an equal neighbor, but restraint is not unlimited. Effective management of maritime differences depends substantially on whether the Philippine government can restrain its military and coast guard. Persistent difficulties in bilateral relations serve neither country’s interests and are particularly damaging to the Philippines’ development. Regional countries should jointly safeguard the region’s hard-won peace and development. Whenever the two sides have moved toward dialogue, certain forces within the Philippines, particularly its military and coast guard, have manufactured incidents to disrupt progress. These forces appear driven less by public welfare than by external powers’ preferences and their own political or institutional interests. If Manila calls for dialogue while allowing these forces to create friction and stoke anti-China sentiment, bilateral communication mechanisms will struggle to function. China and the Philippines are permanent neighbors. Maritime disputes do not change this geographic reality. External military equipment and joint military exercises cannot reverse the regional balance of power. Nor can repeated invocations of a “China threat” narrative resolve the Philippines’ domestic development challenges. Manila may believe that militarization and maritime incidents demonstrate its value as a “frontline platform” for the US and other Western countries, securing stronger security guarantees and economic benefits. Such expectations overlook external powers’ independent strategic calculations. External powers may provide equipment and diplomatic backing while using the Philippines’ geographic location to strengthen their military posture. Their support does not guarantee a willingness to bear the costs of escalation. If a crisis spirals out of control, distant powers can reduce their involvement, leaving the Philippines to face the consequences. History offers repeated warnings about tying national security to another country’s strategic agenda. Manila should weigh that risk carefully. China-Philippines relations stand at a crossroads. Continued tolerance of maritime provocations will invite bolder moves and further damage bilateral ties. The immediate priority for the Marcos government should be to restrain adventurist impulses within its military and coast guard, halt provocations and information operations directed against China, and return to bilateral dialogue and consultation. Only sustained dialogue, supported by restraint and consistent action, can manage differences and stabilize ties. The author is director of the Research Center for International and Regional Studies at the National Institute for South China Sea Studies. opinion@globaltimes.com.cn

item.title: Chinese navy hospital ship arrives in Cote d'Ivoire on medical mission
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16 10:56:00
Local honor guards welcome the Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy hospital ship Auspicious Ark upon its arrival in Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire, Oct. 14, 2026. Auspicious Ark arrived in Abidjan, the economic capital of Cote d'Ivoire, on Wednesday to begin a friendly visit and provide medical services, marking the first visit by a Chinese naval hospital ship to the country. The hospital ship, which is carrying out Mission Harmony-2026, docked at Abidjan at about 10:00 a.m. local time (1000 GMT). (Photo by Yvan Sonh/Xinhua) The Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy hospital ship Auspicious Ark arrived in Abidjan, the economic capital of Cote d'Ivoire, on Wednesday to begin a friendly visit and provide medical services, marking the first visit by a Chinese naval hospital ship to the country. The hospital ship, which is carrying out Mission Harmony-2026, docked at Abidjan at about 10:00 a.m. local time (1000 GMT). Ivorian military and government officials, China's ambassador to Cote d'Ivoire, the defense attache and embassy staff, as well as representatives of the Chinese community and Chinese enterprises welcomed the ship at the port. On board, Chinese naval personnel and civilian staff stood in formation and waved to the welcoming crowd at the port. At the welcoming ceremony, local residents held banners and waved the national flags of China and Cote d'Ivoire to welcome the Chinese naval hospital ship. After the ceremony, the Chief of Staff of the Ivorian Navy boarded the Auspicious Ark and toured the hospital ship. During the seven-day visit, the hospital ship will provide medical treatment for local patients aboard the vessel, while medical personnel will visit the Abidjan Military Hospital and a local university, among other places, for medical exchanges and medical services. The mission will also organize a deck reception to strengthen friendship and mutual trust with the Ivorian side. item.title: 'Forced labor' in Xinjiang's salmon industry, too? The New York Times has lost it: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-15 23:44:00

Photo: VCG In their attacks on Xinjiang-related issues, some Western media outlets are still deliberately presenting themselves as "objective and fair," but the signs of preconceived bias and a narrative assembled to fit a predetermined agenda are all too clear. Recently, The New York Times published a purported in-depth investigative report about the fish farming industry. The article adopts the posture of a "neutral" investigation, citing global research and evidence from multiple sources. It ranges from Peruvian fishing vessels and fishmeal processing plants to offshore aquaculture pens in Norway. Yet in the second half of the article, the focus takes a sharp turn toward the salmon industry in Northwest China's Xinjiang, devoting extensive coverage to recycling familiar allegations such as "forced labor." Read closely, the report reveals a familiar pattern: In their attacks on Xinjiang-related issues, some Western media outlets are still deliberately presenting themselves as "objective and fair," but the signs of preconceived bias and a narrative assembled to fit a predetermined agenda are all too clear. The report offers no evidence from firsthand interviews to support its claims about Xinjiang. Instead, it pieced together much of its narrative from vague attributions with phrases such as "claim," "accuse," and "most likely." By using documented problems in the seafood industry in other parts of the world to shape readers' perceptions in the first half, the article encourages them to assume that the claims made in the second half are equally well substantiated. However, the report provides no solid evidence that similar problems exist in Xinjiang, while packaging subjective speculation as so-called "investigative findings." Such journalistic practices run directly counter to the most basic standards of media credibility. Why are US media outlets willing to lose their credibility just to push out similar fake reports? The real aim, it would appear, is to lend support to Washington's unilateral sanctions targeting Xinjiang. From cotton and tomatoes to sunflower seeds and dumplings, and from solar photovoltaics to polysilicon, the pattern remains the same, with the focus now shifting to Xinjiang's cold-water fish industry: Any competitive industry that benefits Xinjiang's local communities is targeted with the "human rights" cudgel, as negative media coverage is paired with unilateral sanctions to suppress Chinese competitive industries and contain development in China's western regions. It's important to point out that what these sanctions are really aimed at is the employment and development rights of people of all ethnic groups in Xinjiang. In fact, Xinjiang's salmon industry is a prime example of how local resources can be harnessed to turn geographical disadvantages into drivers of development. It is also a tangible achievement of China's campaign to develop its western regions in the new era. Nilka County in the Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture benefits from glacial meltwater flowing down from the Tianshan Mountains. The water remains cold and rich in dissolved oxygen throughout the year, and its excellent quality provides exceptional natural conditions for cold-water fish farming. Technologies such as automated feeding, underwater cleaning robots, and semi-closed recirculating aquaculture systems help minimize pollution, while uneaten feed and fish waste can be processed into organic fertilizer. The farming process emphasizes raising fish without medication and at low stocking densities. Companies in the industry have also obtained multiple international food safety certifications. Their products serve the domestic market and are exported to countries across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Europe. They have even gained access to Singapore, a market known for its stringent food standards. Turning desert landscapes into productive fisheries and snow-capped mountains into a source of premium seafood is an industrial success achieved through Chinese ingenuity and hard work. The benefits to people's livelihoods, brought about by industrial development, are being tangibly enjoyed by the people of all ethnic groups. Under a model that combines leading enterprises, employment in industrial parks and social security, some farming and herding families whose livelihoods have revolved around pastoralism for generations have moved into companies and become industrial workers, earning stable wages. Some herders also receive dividends through equity investments. Many young people have chosen to return to their hometowns for work closer to home. The salmon industry has also spurred the growth of fish-themed agritourism, specialty restaurants, rural tourism, and related businesses, opening up additional sources of income and giving fresh impetus to rural vitalization. These concrete, visible improvements in people's lives stand in stark contrast to the falsehoods propagated by some Western media outlets. Ultimately, no amount of smearing by US media can erase Xinjiang's economic and social development, nor can it stop people of all ethnic groups at the foot of the Tianshan Mountains from striving for a better life. It is hoped that some Western media outlets that pride themselves on being "fair and objective" will drop their self-deceptive tactics and go to Xinjiang to see the real production scenes for themselves, listen to workers on the ground describe their own experiences, and gain a firsthand understanding of what human rights really mean to the people of all ethnic groups in Xinjiang - and what rights they genuinely enjoy and deserve to have respected.
